shortDescription: Oracle's NYSE:ORCL first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings results proved the potential of its infrastructure as a service strategy as cloud infrastructure revenue surged 121% year over year to $7.4B.Shares initially popped up about 7% during post-market trading on Thursday. children: proved the potential of its infrastructure as a service strategy as cloud infrastructure revenue surged 121% year over year to $7.4B.

Shares initially popped up about 7% during post-market trading on Thursday. However, by noon trading on Friday, shares had increased less than 1%. Despite the lukewarm next-day reaction in the market, analysts across the board were positive on the results.
J.P. Morgan reiterated its Outperform rating and $200 price target.

"The company delivered to expectations with total revenue growth of +30% y/y, tracking above the guide on triple-digit growth in Cloud Infrastructure, and RPO building a further $26B sequentially," said J.P. Morgan analyst Samik Chatterjee in a Friday investor note.

"The strength was evident across multiple drivers: 1) Capacity delivery of 850 MW in the quarter, nearly three times what was delivered in all of F4Q26 and none of it from the flagship sites that have attracted investor scrutiny, which in our view demonstrates the diversification of the build-out and mitigates risk to the medium-term outlook from any single site delay; 2) More than $30B of new AI contracts, primarily booked on prepay or bring-your-own-hardware (BYOH) structures; and 3) Operating leverage and discipline that helped hold PF operating margin flat at ~42% despite the expected step-down in gross margin, reinforcing our view that operating margin, rather than gross margin, is the appropriate lens as infrastructure becomes a larger share of the mix," he added.
Meanwhile, Jefferies reiterated its Buy rating and $290 price target, highlighting Oracle's significant backlog.

"Backlog was $664B (46% y/y growth), up 4% q/q ($26B q/q) vs. 15% in F4Q26 and 6% q/q in F3Q26," said Jefferies analyst Brent Thill in a note. "On a y/y basis, backlog decelerated vs. 363% y/y growth in F4Q. The backlog growth was driven by >$30B of additional AI cloud contracts booked in F1Q. Mgmt indicated that based on the structuring of those new contracts, there is no incremental impact on its plans to raise capital."
Similarly, Citi reiterated its Buy rating and hefty $330 price target.

"Oracle delivered more than 300,000 GPUs during the quarter while adding 850MW of datacenter capacity and older GPUs seeing 20% premium on renewed and resold contracts," Citi analysts said in a note. Roughly half of RPO is expected to flow into revenue over the next 36 months, with RPO conversion to revenue expected to accelerate. Multicloud DB cloud grew 353% y/y, and multicloud customers grew 180% y/y, with multicloud DB regions reaching 70. They also completed their $20B at-the-market equity issuance in Q1."

title: Oracle's Q1 proves potential of IaaS strategy as cloud infra surges 121%: analysts
